metaDescription: Count characters and see how many are left against any limits you set, such as SMS 160 or a 280 character post. Free, runs in your browser.
intro: Count characters as you paste and see how many are left against one or more limits you choose, such as 160 for SMS or 280 for a post.
why:
Many fields have a hard limit: an SMS, a meta description, a button label, a post. Counting by eye fails, and word processors count differently from the platform you paste into.

This counter shows characters the way people see them, plus code points, UTF-16 length and UTF-8 bytes, so you can tell why two tools disagree. You can set several limits at once and see the room left on each. Nothing leaves your browser.
howTo: Enter one or more limits, separated by commas.
Read the remaining characters for each limit.
Tick the trim option if spaces at the ends should not count.

faq.q: Why do emoji count differently in other tools?
faq.a: An emoji is one character to a reader but two or more UTF-16 units and several bytes. This tool shows all the counts so you can compare.
No. SMS splits messages at 160 characters in the GSM alphabet and 70 once any other character appears, and long messages use smaller parts. Use it as a first check.
